subject: Rebaseline proposal: split-delivery MAP & revised close dates
content:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chang <mike.chang@atlasretail.com>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft + evaluation windows — proposal to reduce close risk

Mike / Lydia,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion I pulled together an initial mutual action plan and a couple of options to reduce close-date risk given the procurement timeline you described.

Key points:
- Two-track MAP: (A) Core production delivery (integration + internal eval) and (B) Optional pilot features + optimization.
- Staggered acceptance gates so Atlas can start internal evals earlier while we finish the remaining integration tasks.
- Suggested new close window: move from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-15 for final-signature conditional on completing Gate 2 acceptance by 2026-10-08.

I attached a one-page MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx) and an evaluation checklist (eval-checklist.pdf) so your procurement and technical teams can see the specific acceptance criteria and timelines.

Would you be open to the split-delivery approach (allows Atlas to begin evals and pilots earlier) or do you prefer we hold to the single-delivery plan? If split, we can commit to the two milestones above and update the SOW to reflect partial acceptance and invoice staging.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call with procurement and engineering to walk through the acceptance criteria.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

---

From: Mike Chang <mike.chang@atlasretail.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@atlasretail.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + evaluation windows — proposal to reduce close risk

Mateo,

Thanks for the materials — the checklist is helpful. Two items I want to flag that are causing us internal slippage:
1) Legal needs an additional week to review the new data handling language (we've got a backlog).
2) Our analytics team requested a second test dataset because the first one surfaced a memory edge case in our pipeline.

If we slide the close 2 weeks to give Legal time and to run the extra dataset, that should be sufficient. The split-delivery approach sounds reasonable — it might actually help unblock analytics earlier.

Can you confirm whether the Gate 1 deliverable is sufficient for our analytics team to start parallel testing? If not, what minimal artifact would be required?

—Mike
Mike Chang
CTO | Atlas Retail
mike.chang@atlasretail.com

---

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + evaluation windows — proposal to reduce close risk

Mateo / Laura,

Looping you both in with a proposed risk-reduction play:

Proposed change (split-delivery, lightweight artifact for Gate 1):
- Gate 1 (2 weeks after initial deploy): deliver an API endpoint with a 5K-row sample response set + download of KV-cache snapshot and basic latency profile. That should be enough for Atlas analytics to run their memory/regression tests.
- Gate 2 (full acceptance): full-scale dataset run and production hardening checklist.
- Adjustment to invoicing: 40% on Gate 1 acceptance, 60% on Gate 2 final sign-off.

I also recommend we add a short escalation clause in the MAP that kicks to Laura if either gate misses by more than 3 business days — keeps momentum and gives the customer a clear path to accelerate approvals.

Attaching a quick edit to the MAP (I added the artifact definition) and a pricing summary for the split approach.

Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: MAP_v2.xlsx (edited), pricing-summary.csv

---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chang <mike.chang@atlasretail.com>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft + evaluation windows — proposal to reduce close risk

Mike / Lydia,

Thanks — Grace and I iterated on the MAP and added the Gate 1 artifact you asked about. Summary of changes:
- Gate 1 artifact: API endpoint + 5K sample CSV + KV-cache snapshot + performance baseline (p95/p50)
- New proposed close date: 2026-10-15 conditional on Gate 2 acceptance by 2026-10-08
- Invoicing staged as Grace suggested (40/60) and we added an escalation ownership (Laura) if timelines slip >3 business days.

I attached MAP_v2.xlsx and the eval-checklist.pdf for you to circulate with Procurement and Analytics. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min alignment call tomorrow (Wed) to walk the analytics team through the Gate 1 artifact so they can confirm it's sufficient.

Next steps:
1) Atlas confirmation on Gate 1 artifact adequacy (reply ok/no-ok)
2) Legal to confirm sign-off timeline (Lydia — any update on when Legal can review?)
3) If ok, I will update the SOW and send the DocuSign bundle for the staged invoice schedule.

Best,
Mateo

Attachment stubs: MAP_v2.xlsx, eval-checklist.pdf

---

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chang <mike.chang@atlasretail.com>, Lydia Park <lydia.park@atlasretail.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Final: agreed split-delivery MAP and updated close schedule (next steps)

Mike / Lydia — thanks for confirming on the call earlier. Quick summary and next steps so we have a single record:

Agreed:
- Split-delivery MAP accepted by Atlas (Gate 1 artifact meets analytics needs).
- Legal (Lydia) will complete review by EOD 2026-09-20; if additional items are requested we will treat them as redline-only and not block Gate 1 acceptance.
- Close window updated to 2026-10-15 with Gate 2 acceptance target of 2026-10-08.
- Invoice schedule: 40% on Gate 1 acceptance, remainder on Gate 2 final sign-off.
- Escalation: Laura Bennett is primary Redwood exec for timeline exceptions; she will engage if any gate misses more than 3 business days.

Action items:
- Atlas: confirm Legal completion date (Lydia) and confirm internal resource for the final full-scale run (Rajiv).
- Redwood: issue updated SOW and DocuSign bundle by 2026-09-12 (Mateo).
- Joint: schedule a Gate 1 handoff demo the week of 2026-09-13.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx, eval-checklist.pdf, pricing-summary.csv (stubs)

If anyone needs a shorter SLA on the Gate 1 demo, we can compress the handoff into a 20-min focused session for Rajiv.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Atlas into pilot.

Mateo Alvarez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
